Both competing transfer approaches are substantial. Tus over multipart is a meaningful analogous composition; concatenation/per-request checksums and measured future concurrency are bounded opportunities. Scope does not require a catalog of every uploader or a deployed service. The conditional recommendation has investigated mechanisms and discriminating checks, not vacuous caution.

The synthetic 'Other criticism' rejection does not refer to an actual additional critic finding and is not counted as one. Exact plan dispositions are enumerated.

The checksum extension stays available conditionally; omission of a mandatory per-PATCH feature is not a scope loss because the original source made it optional.

No transfer tests were required to run in this research-only fixture. Actual checks are source inspection and reported reveal/hash/JSON checks; reviewers independently verified frozen identities, not product behavior. No invented test or real upload is credited.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Tus 1.0.0 core; bytes
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Authoritative nonnegative integer offset; mismatch returns 409 without mutation; success acknowledges processed/stored range, not independent final-object verification.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Tus extension support
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Creation, expiration, checksum, termination and concatenation are optional; auth/durable state/UUID create semantics are not implied by extension advertisement.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Tus expiration; absolute 30 days
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Upload-Expires on PATCH and creation when known; known expired resource uses 410. Thirty days is a chosen policy, not a protocol default.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Tus PATCH-body integrity
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Advertised algorithms; at least sha1 if implemented; verifies request body, not assembled full-file hash.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart IDs and parts
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Upload ID + per-part ETag/number manifest; numbered parts assembled in ascending order; same-number replacement; incomplete operations differ from object completion.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS ListParts; 1,000 results
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Paginate; omitted unfinished calls are not failed calls; retain own completion manifest. Listing alone cannot settle operation uncertainty.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS part sizes/count; MiB/GiB
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: 5 MiB–5 GiB with last-part minimum exception; 10,000 parts. 6 GiB gives 384 full parts; 20 MiB gives 16+4 MiB. Not vendor/performance proof.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart checksums
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Overview states a broad checksum rule; dedicated integrity guidance scopes the important note to composite/part-level checksums. Proposed consecutive numbering is safe regardless; broader explanatory applicability is not settled by the overview alone.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: ETag and full-file SHA-256
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Multipart ETag not assumed full-file MD5; storage-validated strong digest must describe the exact full byte sequence, or read-back SHA-256; CRC/composite cannot substitute silently.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS multipart SHA-256 versus full-object CRC
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: SHA-256 composite; CRC64NVME/CRC32/CRC32C support full-object type. Algorithm/type/initiation/completion/retrieval must be qualified together.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS SSE-KMS permissions
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: GenerateDataKey and Decrypt conditions; checksum access depends on permissions. Exact mode and permission path gate implementation.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS SSE-C completion checksums
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Overview's checksum availability claim is supported in its context. API headers are conditional on checksum use/policy and SSE-C is unsupported in directory buckets. No blanket claim about the unspecified vendor is made.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: AWS in-flight UploadPart
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Unknown is not Failed; prevent same-number overlap and completion, settle or retire ID, preserve cleanup queue. Already in-flight requests can finish after abort; repeat cleanup/verify.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Remote object versus HTTP result
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Actual operation success plus target/size/session checks required; AWS 200 can embed error. Final does not use HTTP status alone or cancel intent as proof of committed/aborted state.

consequential_claim_checks.subject: Rust S3 client v1.69.0; 2025-01-16
consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: Dated maintainer announcement and third-party caveat; relevant only if SDK is used. No current CRC default or deployed library pin is invented.

consequential_claim_checks.governing_conditions: One original open report with mutable tag and unresolved cause; cannot infer universal defect, known fix or version applicability.

Draft said query known storage state but did not define how absence from a list fails to settle an unfinished request. Final adds per-operation states, no overlap/commit while unknown, settlement or retirement and retained cleanup ownership. Conservative retirement is explicitly a design choice.

The proposed sequential part numbering is safe and no material recommendation depends on nonconsecutive full-object uploads; exact mode applicability remains a qualification issue.

The 'Other criticism or a need to reverse the Tus recommendation' row is a synthetic caveat, not a third criticism actually found in critique.md. It is not credited as a criticism disposition or as evidence that Tus is suitable.

independent_primary_sources.title: CompleteMultipartUpload API reference
independent_primary_sources.version: Current API reference; S3 API namespace 2006-03-01; document edition not pinned
independent_primary_sources.observation: Completion requires successful interpretation of the operation, not merely HTTP 200: the body can contain an error. SDKs handle embedded errors. SSE-C checksum header requirements have operation conditions and directory-bucket exceptions. The final requires operation success plus object/session checks and leaves exact adapter qualification open; it does not equate 200 with success.
independent_primary_sources.conditions: KMS permission and SSE-C paths depend on selected mode; SSE-C is unsupported for directory buckets. A completed multipart SHA-256 response can be derived from part checksums.
independent_primary_sources.domains: AWS CompleteMultipartUpload; exact compatible-vendor response/permission contract remains UNKNOWN.
independent_primary_sources.excerpt: a 200 OK response can contain either a success or an error.

independent_primary_sources.title: AbortMultipartUpload API reference
independent_primary_sources.version: Current API reference; no document edition shown
independent_primary_sources.observation: Already in-flight part requests may succeed or fail after abort. Repeated abort may be necessary; checking that no parts remain is the API's cleanup verification. This supports preserving the cleanup queue after retiring or canceling an uncertain upload.
independent_primary_sources.conditions: An abort response alone cannot prove all storage has been released during an in-flight race. Exact provider behavior must be established.
independent_primary_sources.domains: AWS abort/list operations, not generalized vendor behavior.
independent_primary_sources.excerpt: it might be necessary to abort a given multipart upload multiple times

independent_primary_sources.title: Checking object integrity for data uploads in Amazon S3
independent_primary_sources.version: Current User Guide; no semantic edition shown
locators: Full object and composite checksum types
independent_primary_sources.observation: The dedicated table confirms multipart SHA-256 is composite and full-object CRC algorithms differ. Its consecutive-number note is explicitly scoped to composite/part-level checksums, whereas the overview uses broader wording. It also warns that some completion checksum headers can be accepted without validation when the algorithm was not selected at initiation.
independent_primary_sources.conditions: Always qualify initiation, type, algorithm, completion, retrieval and encryption as a joined contract. Final's sequential numbering is safe; its generic all-checksums explanation should not be read as resolving narrower API applicability.
independent_primary_sources.domains: AWS multipart versus single PutObject distinction; no arbitrary vendor guarantee.
